title: Anthropic adapter config
description: Configuration of the anthropic-adapter command, which serves the OpenAI Responses API on top of the Anthropic Messages API. Every key is optional; the defaults are shown. No credential is stored here: the caller sends it as a Bearer token or x-api-key header and the adapter forwards it.

base_url.description: Anthropic API base URL. /v1/messages is appended.

auth_header.description: How the token the caller sent is passed upstream. bearer sends Authorization: Bearer <token>, the form Anthropic documents; it carries an API key or a Workload Identity Federation access token. x-api-key sends the legacy header, for a proxy that expects it.

beta.description: Values joined into the anthropic-beta header.

credential_file.description: Path of a credential file written by the claude-auth command (a Claude Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise sign-in). Absolute, or starting with ~/. When set, the adapter sends the access token stored in it as the upstream credential, reads the file on every request (so a refresh by claude-auth needs no restart), never writes it, and ignores the credential the caller sent. Empty forwards the caller's credential. Anthropic does not document this sign-in and limits subscription credentials to its own applications; see cmd/anthropic-adapter/README.md.

system_prefix.description: Text sent as the first system block of every request, as a block of its own, before the caller's instructions. Empty sends nothing extra. DISCOURAGED. On 2026-10-08 a Claude subscription token (credential_file) was answered 429 'Error' without a system prompt, and 200 for tiny requests whose system prompt was "You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude." But a real session turn was then refused with 400 'Third-party apps now draw from your extra usage, not your plan limits' (extra usage was disabled for the organization), so the key does not avoid third-party billing. It claims an identity the program does not have, so it is off by default and the choice is the account owner's. For Claude in this harness use an API key instead.

expiry_margin_ms.description: How long before its stored expiry a credential_file token already counts as expired, so a request is not sent with a token that ends in flight. Applies only with credential_file. Keep it equal to claude-auth's expiry_margin_ms.

extra_headers.description: Headers added to every upstream request, for a gateway or endpoint that wants more than the adapter sets. authorization, x-api-key, anthropic-version, anthropic-beta, content-type, content-length and host cannot be set here: they come from auth_header, beta and anthropic_version.

extra_body.description: Top-level fields merged into every /v1/messages request body, each value sent as written (for example metadata, top_k, stop_sequences, service_tier, or cache_control {"type":"ephemeral","ttl":"1h"}). Fields the adapter builds from the client request (model, max_tokens, system, messages, tools, tool_choice, stream, temperature, top_p, thinking, output_config) are refused. cache_control conflicts with cache.automatic and is refused when both are set.

request_timeout_ms.description: Deadline for one upstream request, including the whole stream.

stream_retry.description: Retry of a streaming request that fails with an error event before any output reached the caller. An HTTP error status is not retried here: it goes to the caller, whose own provider_retry handles it.

error_types.description: Anthropic error types that are retried.

default_max_tokens.description: max_tokens sent when the request has no max_output_tokens. Anthropic requires the field.

unsupported_fields.description: What to do with a request field that has no Anthropic equivalent and changes behavior (for example top_logprobs). ignore drops it and lists it in the X-Adapter-Ignored-Fields response header. previous_response_id, conversation, background and hosted tools are always rejected.

synthesize_missing_tool_results.description: Answer a function_call that has no function_call_output with an error tool_result. Anthropic rejects a tool_use without a result.

missing_tool_result_text.default: No result was recorded for this tool call.

invalid_arguments_key.description: function_call arguments that are not a JSON object are sent as {key: original string}.

strip_schema_keywords.description: Keywords removed from the top level of every tool's input schema before it is sent. Anthropic answers 400 'input_schema does not support oneOf, allOf, or anyOf at the top level', and the harness's fetch, task, memory and process tools use them to say 'one of these fields is required'. Only the top level is changed, nested schemas are not. The caller still validates each call against its full schema, so the rule is enforced there; the model no longer sees it. Each removal is listed in the X-Adapter-Ignored-Fields response header as tools.<name>.<keyword>. An empty list sends schemas unchanged.

log.description: What the adapter writes to stderr when an upstream call fails. Without it a failure reaches the caller as one short message and the response headers that explain it (request id, Retry-After, rate-limit headers) are lost. The request's headers are never logged by value, so the credential cannot reach the log; only their names are.

upstream_errors.description: Log one line per failed upstream call: an HTTP error status, an error event in a stream, a non-stream body for a stream request, or an error body behind HTTP 200.

body_bytes.description: How much of the response body (or the error event's message) to log, on one line. 0 logs none.

headers.description: Response header names to log, matched without regard to case. A trailing * matches a prefix.

cache.description: Prompt-caching breakpoints. All off by default: a cache write costs 1.25x (5 minutes) or 2x (1 hour) the input price, so caching only pays when the same prefix is reused within the TTL. Anthropic allows 4 breakpoints per request; these four switches use at most 4. Prompts below the model's minimum cacheable length are processed without caching and without an error.

automatic.description: Send the top-level cache_control, which marks the last cacheable block of the request.

system.description: Mark the last system block. The cached prefix covers the tools as well.

history.description: Mark the last block that comes from a real conversation item, skipping system or developer text appended after it. Use it instead of automatic when the caller appends changing context (a timestamp, state) at the end of every request: the automatic breakpoint would land on that text and never hit.

models.description: Per-model rules. The first entry whose match regex fits the request model wins; otherwise default_profile applies.

match.description: Regular expression tested against the model name.

thinking.description: none sends no thinking parameter. adaptive sends thinking {type: adaptive} and output_config.effort. budget sends thinking {type: enabled, budget_tokens} for models that still need it.

display.description: thinking.display to send. Empty sends none, except that a request with reasoning.summary selects summarized.

default_effort.description: Effort used when the request has no reasoning.effort. none turns thinking off for this request.

effort_map.description: Responses effort to output_config.effort. Missing keys use the defaults (minimal and low to low, medium to medium, high to high, xhigh to xhigh, max to max).

effort_budget.description: Responses effort to budget_tokens in budget mode. Defaults: minimal 1024, low 2048, medium 8192, high 16384, xhigh 24576, max 32000.

mid_conversation_system.description: Send system and developer messages that follow the first turn as role=system. When false they become user messages.
